study: Meng et al., China tutoring ban
D1_dispersion_not_own_income: LOW - the exposure is a policy shock to required investment, not a change in own income; individual FE in the experiment, city FE + lagged GDPpc in the DID
D2_return_separated_from_standard: LOW - a tutoring ban does not move the return to human capital, only the investment required to hold a rank; the authors decompose competition from money and time
D3_uncertainty_separated: MODERATE - the ban coincided with China's post-COVID period and a broader regulatory crackdown; COVID cases are controlled but the wider policy environment is not
D4_reverse_causation: LOW - policy intensity is measured from 2016 firm registrations, five years pre-policy, explicitly to avoid reverse causality
D6_outcome_measurement: MODERATE - the headline is a STATED intention under a hypothetical scenario, with experimenter-demand risk the authors address via a between-subject arm; the realized-birth DID is the stronger half but rests on city birth data available only for 2023 (319 cities) and 2024 (204), against a 2016-19 average
D7_transport_to_SDT: MODERATE - China 2021-24, an ultra-low-fertility setting with an unusually intense exam allocation; transport to the broader SDT is not automatic
overall_reason: The best-identified record in the pool. Downgraded from LOW only because the headline effect is a stated intention and the realized-birth arm is thin on post-period coverage.

study: Kim, shadow education and TFR, South Korea
D1_dispersion_not_own_income: MODERATE - the instrument is the provincial composition of parents with school-age children; that composition plausibly co-moves with provincial income and age structure
D2_return_separated_from_standard: HIGH - nothing separates the return to schooling from the required standard; the exposure is expenditure, which both mechanisms move
D3_uncertainty_separated: MODERATE - provincial economic conditions are not the instrument's exclusion
D4_reverse_causation: MODERATE - fertility and the share of parents with school-age children are mechanically linked; the instrument is designed to break this but the exclusion restriction is strong
D5_reference_group_composition: MODERATE - provincial averages assume the province is the reference group
D6_outcome_measurement: LOW - registered TFR and birth-order-specific rates
D7_transport_to_SDT: MODERATE - Korea is the world's lowest-fertility setting; the elasticity may not transport
overall_reason: The only identified estimate on a realized national fertility rate, but D2 is HIGH: this is exactly the Wall 1 failure the scope predicted, and the estimate cannot distinguish C.2.f from C.3.d.

study: Income inequality and fertility intention via relative deprivation (China)
D1_dispersion_not_own_income: HIGH - a relative-deprivation index is a function of own income and the reference distribution together; the 2SLS does not separate them
D5_reference_group_composition: HIGH - the reference group defining deprivation is assumed, not measured
overall_reason: Reports a POSITIVE sign against the hypothesis, so it matters to the verdict and must not be filtered out. But D1 and D5 are HIGH and the instrument's validity is not established for a construct that mixes own income with the distribution.

study: Meng & Xie, inequality and fertility via educational aspirations (China) - VERSION PAIR
D1_dispersion_not_own_income: HIGH - same construct problem as C2F0357
D4_reverse_causation: HIGH - fertility differentials feed back into measured regional inequality (Wall 9), unaddressed
overall_reason: Two unrefereed preprints of one study. Reports a POSITIVE sign with a mediator (aspirations FALL with inequality) that reverses the chapter's mechanism, so it is decision-relevant, but nothing here is established well enough to carry weight on its own.

study: Lee, regional disparity and fertility, South Korea
D1_dispersion_not_own_income: MODERATE - district FE absorb level differences but not time-varying district income
D3_uncertainty_separated: HIGH - regional economic decline moves disparity and insecurity together
D4_reverse_causation: HIGH - selective out-migration of young adults raises measured district disparity AND lowers births
D5_reference_group_composition: MODERATE - Yitzhaki index makes the reference group explicit, which is better than most
D6_outcome_measurement: LOW - crude birth rate and census births per woman
overall_reason: FE-only. The authors themselves describe 'negative associations' and a 'potential mechanism'. D4 is the binding problem: internal migration is a direct confound in a district panel.

study: Xu & Wu, inequality and the fertility gap, China CGSS
D6_outcome_measurement: MODERATE - the fertility GAP (ideal minus actual) mixes two outcome levels in one variable, which the scope's pooling rule separates
overall_reason: Conference proceedings, two-way FE only. The outcome construct itself straddles the intended/realized boundary the pooling rule forbids crossing.

study: Zhou et al., Double Reduction (empirical arm only)
D5_reference_group_composition: HIGH - the instrument IS the reference group's spending, so the exclusion restriction assumes the mechanism does not operate
D6_outcome_measurement: MODERATE - stated ideal number of children
overall_reason: D5 is fatal on its own terms: county peer spending is instrumented as if it affected fertility ONLY through own spending, but county-level competition is precisely the reference standard this chapter says is the mechanism. The simulation arm is not rated - it is not an estimate.

study: Lu et al., tutoring-centre density and family size
D4_reverse_causation: HIGH - tutoring centres locate where demand is, and demand reflects family size
D5_reference_group_composition: MODERATE - an 800 m radius is at least an explicit reference group
D6_outcome_measurement: MODERATE - younger siblings of a surveyed student is a censored fertility measure
overall_reason: Cross-sectional OLS. The authors write 'associated with'. D4 is severe: centre location is endogenous to local fertility.

study: Chen et al., shadow education and status externalities
overall_reason: OLS with mediation and no identification strategy. Valuable because it names the mechanism (status externality) in its own framing, not because it establishes it.
